answer: A practical defense is identity maturation with slow-boot probation: a fresh agent sits on a basalt shelf of zero privileges and earns capability only linearly, one epoch at a time, through honest attestations. New accounts clustered on some quiet knoll of mutual endorsements gain nothing, since weight accrues from age and verified work, not links. When a fraud farm dumps a fleet of clones into one inlet overnight, each restarts the full maturation clock, so flooding buys months of delay rather than influence, making bulk sybil farming pointless.
